# Deploy a service
## Promote an image
A deployment promotes an immutable image digest from staging to production. Run the smoke check against staging before promotion. Keep the previous production digest in the deployment record. A tag can move; a digest identifies the image that was reviewed.
## Roll back
To roll back a service, select the previous production digest and create a new deployment. Rollback does not undo database migrations. A migration that deletes a column must wait until the old application version no longer reads it.
## Check readiness
The readiness endpoint returns HTTP 200 only after configuration is loaded and the database connection succeeds. A live process is not sufficient to receive traffic. The load balancer stops sending new requests to instances that fail readiness.

# Rebuild the documentation index
## Create a new generation
Create a new search table when the embedding model or chunking rules change. Record the model digest, vector dimensions, query instruction and corpus hash. Do not mix vectors from different model builds in the same generation.
## Switch readers
Load the new generation and run the saved developer questions before changing the active generation setting. Keep the previous table until readers have switched. A successful table load does not establish that relevant documents are retrieved.
## Remove a document
Delete every chunk ID belonging to the removed document from each active search generation. Removing a page from the website does not remove its stored vectors. Run the deletion check before accepting another search request.

# Rotate a service API key
## Prepare rotation
Create a replacement key with the same required scope and store it in the secret manager. Deploy the replacement to callers before revoking the old key. Never place either key in search documents, logs or model prompts.
## Revoke the old key
After all callers use the replacement key, revoke the old key and check that an old-key request receives HTTP 401. A new-key request must still succeed. A configuration rollout alone does not establish that the old credential was revoked.
## Limit key scope
A documentation reader key can read published pages but cannot update the search index. The indexing job uses a separate credential. A metadata filter in a search request does not replace the service's authorization check.

# Operate an embedding job
## Retry an interrupted batch
Each input chunk has a stable ID. Retrying an interrupted batch upserts the same IDs instead of appending duplicate rows. The integration commits each document separately, so an error can leave an earlier part of the batch written.
## Respect model limits
Batch text within the embedding model's context limit. Character-based splitting is not a token limit. If the embedding service rejects an input, reduce the chunk size and rebuild the affected generation rather than silently truncating the document.
## Read the chart
The embedding job report includes latency by batch size. The chart shows one supplied example run, not a service-level objective. Read the percentile label before comparing bars: the median and the tail describe different parts of the run.

# Deploy a data transformation
## Stage the transform
Write transformed rows to a staging table and compare row counts and null rates before switching the reporting view. A successful SQL statement does not establish that the transformation preserves the intended business meaning.
## Roll back a view
Restore the reporting view to its previous table when a transformation produces incorrect rows. Retain the old table until downstream reports have been checked. This process does not roll back application services or their container images.

# Publish a dataset description
## Describe a column
A dataset description names the column, its unit, the update schedule and the owning team. Give timestamps a timezone. Similar column names do not establish that two datasets use the same unit or join key.
## Remove stale entries
Remove catalog entries for deleted datasets after checking references from saved reports. Reindex the changed descriptions so search stops returning the old columns. A catalog deletion does not itself delete a physical database table.
